content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli is the edible flower head of Brassica oleracea var. italica, widely cultivated in temperate regions. When cooked, broccoli retains a bright green color, a mild flavor and a slightly crisp texture. It is used in side dishes, soups, salads and Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli belongs to the same family as cabbage, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts and kale.
It is believed to have been domesticated in the Mediterranean over 2,000 years ago.
Raw broccoli contains more vitamin C than oranges, though some is lost during cooking.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for potential anticancer effects.
In Japan, broccoli is often served as “tenkatsu” – a battered and fried piece.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked broccoli provides a substantial portion of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Phytochemical compounds
items.content: Sulforaphane and other glucosinolates have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Broccoli is low in calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to cruciferous vegetables, including broccoli.

items.title: Nutrient loss with cooking
items.content: Prolonged boiling can reduce vitamin C and some phytochemicals.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Broccoli may cause increased gas in some individuals due to its raffinose content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steam broccoli for 5‑7 minutes until tender, add it to soups, stews, pasta, salads, or serve as a side dish with olive oil, lemon and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh broccoli in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or container, where it stays crisp for up to 5 days. Store cooked broccoli in an airtight container in the fridge for no more than 3‑4 days.
